name: Supernode data centre campus

address.note: From master.csv. QLD cadastre (source 7): 81, 83 and 87-93 Kremzow Road = Lot 121 M31114 (161,874 m2), zoned Industry - General industry precinct (source 10). Private Energy Partners' schematic site map (May 2026, source 9) places the 'Supernode BESS site boundary' on the south side of Kremzow Road directly north of the South Pine Switchyard, i.e. this lot; the mapped area is entirely BESS (built and 'in development') plus substations, with no data centre footprint shown. Council's DA dataset maps the BESS permit DA/2023/1419 to a point in Lot 3 SP213172 (26 Cribb Road, ~1.3 km south), so the DA may span several lots; not verified. The 30 ha campus lot list is not published.

lat.note: Geocoded 2026-09-27 from '83 Kremzow Road, Brendale QLD 4500' with the ArcGIS World Geocoder (PointAddress, score 100).

builder.note: No data centre builder. BESS designed/procured/built by Quinbrook affiliate Private Energy Partners (source 9).

mw_it.note: Per-building IT MW not published. Private Energy Partners (Quinbrook affiliate) states '500 MW-IT potential data centre capacity on-site' and the precinct 'is capable of hosting 500MW of capacity' - a site-potential figure, not an approved or designed load, so not entered as the value.

mw_grid.note: Quinbrook 2022: 'up to 800 MWs of power supply capacity' via South Pine substation (three HV connections) - site supply capacity shared with the BESS (780 MW / 3,073 MWh across Stages 1-3, source 9), not DC demand.

cost_aud_m.note: Quinbrook 2022: 'up to $2.5 billion when fully constructed' (whole campus incl. BESS). Later figures: 'more than A$3 billion of investment is projected for the Supernode precinct' across all stages (source 9); BESS Stages 1-3 'expected to exceed A$1.4 billion' (source 9). No data centre-only cost published; the DC share is at most ~A$1.1-1.6bn by subtraction, which is an inference, not a stated figure.

authority.value: City of Moreton Bay (Moreton Bay Regional Council)
authority.note: Quinbrook (8 Jul 2022) claimed 'local planning permissions from Moreton Bay Regional Council'. Site is not in a Priority Development Area (PDA DAs in council's dataset are at The Mill, Petrie) and no state/ministerial approval pathway was found.

pathway.note: No DC approval found. Under the MBRC Planning Scheme (V4 eff. 29 Jan 2020 and V7 eff. 30 Oct 2024), Table 5.5.7.3.1 Industry zone - General industry precinct: 'Research and technology industry' (the Planning Regulation 2017 use term whose examples include computer server facilities - from the Regulation's definition, not re-read in this pass) and 'Low impact industry' are 'Assessable development - Code assessment ... In all instances' (source 10). A data centre building on Lot 121 M31114 would therefore need a council development permit, which would appear in the DA dataset. The only Supernode permit found is DA/2023/1419 (RoL - subdivision by lease and access easement; MCU and Building Works - Development Permit for Battery Storage Facility), lodged 2023-04-18, approved 2023-11-17 (source 8) - a BESS approval, not a DC approval.

reference.note: No data centre DA exists in the City of Moreton Bay open DA dataset (16,519 applications lodged Feb 2016 - 2026, queried 2026-09-27): no application on or intersecting Lot 121 M31114 at all; none mentioning 'data', 'server' or Supernode; the only 'research and technology industry' permits nearby are unrelated (DA/34673/2017/V2N, 2017, ~1 km north). BESS permit: DA/2023/1419. DA/36991/2018/V2L is an unrelated residential preliminary approval.

determined.note: No DC approval date. The 2022 'local planning permissions' claim (source 1) is not matched by any council record; PEP describes 2022 only as 'Masterplan & regulatory approvals - Integrated campus vision confirmed for data + battery storage' (source 9). Even the BESS needed its own permit in 2023, so the 2022 'permissions' were not a development permit for the built works.

jobs_construction.note: No jobs figures found for the data centre. PEP community hub says only that the project 'has created, and will continue to create, jobs in both the construction and operational phases' (source 9).

construction_start.note: 'Construction begins onsite in June 2024' (source 9) refers to BESS Stage 1; no data centre construction found. Quinbrook's Supernode DC project page shows 'Status Construction' (source 9) but gives no DC works; the May 2026 site map shows only BESS.

construction_end.note: BESS Stage 1 (260 MW / 619 MWh) commercial operations Feb 2026; Stage 2 July 2026 (Stages 1+2 = 520 MW / 1,858 MWh); Stage 3 (Stanwell offtake) under construction (sources 4, 9). No data centre timing; Baxtel's 2028-2031 is unsourced.
